skill.name: resume-tailoring
skill.description: Use when adapting a resume to a specific job description to pass ATS keyword screens and earn a recruiter's attention.
whenToUse: Customizing a base resume for a particular job posting before applying
Matching resume keywords to a job description for ATS compatibility
Rewriting flat duty statements into quantified, results-driven bullets
Reordering or trimming experience to lead with the most relevant work

keyConcepts.explanation: Applicant tracking systems rank resumes by how well they match the job description's terms. Mirror the posting's exact skills, tools, and titles (within reason) so the resume surfaces in searches.
A generic resume rarely matches any single posting well. Tailoring means adjusting the summary, skills, and bullet emphasis per role so the most relevant qualifications appear first.
Strong bullets pair an action verb with a measurable outcome (percent, dollars, time, scale). Numbers make impact concrete and credible versus vague responsibility lists.
Use the posting's terminology where it is genuinely true of your experience. Over-stuffing irrelevant keywords backfires with recruiters and can read as dishonest.
Recruiters skim top-to-bottom in seconds. Put the experience, skills, and achievements most aligned to the target role near the top of each section.

apiReference.purpose: Read the job description and list required skills, tools, qualifications, and repeated keywords.
apiReference.example: Highlight must-haves vs nice-to-haves and note exact phrasing of titles/tools

apiReference.purpose: Match each requirement to a concrete project or achievement you can honestly claim.
apiReference.example: Requirement: 'led cross-functional teams' -> bullet about coordinating 3 teams on launch X

apiReference.purpose: Convert duties into action-verb + result bullets with numbers wherever possible.
apiReference.example: Before: 'Responsible for sales.' After: 'Grew regional sales 28% YoY ($1.2M) in 4 quarters.'

apiReference.purpose: Mirror the posting's terms in your summary and skills, and use standard ATS-friendly section headers.
apiReference.example: Use 'Work Experience', 'Skills', 'Education'; avoid tables/graphics that ATS can't parse

apiReference.purpose: Lead with the most relevant roles and bullets; cut content that doesn't support this job.
apiReference.example: Move the most relevant role's bullets to the top; drop unrelated older roles to one line

gotchas: Never invent skills or metrics to match keywords — fabrication surfaces in interviews and reference checks
Avoid tables, columns, text boxes, and images; many ATS parsers mangle them and drop your content
Match the posting's exact term ('Customer Success' vs 'Account Management') rather than a synonym for ATS hits
Keyword stuffing hurts once a human reads it; keep keywords inside truthful, specific bullets
Tailor every application; reusing one resume for many roles dilutes relevance for all of them
Save and submit as the requested format (usually PDF or .docx) so formatting and parsing stay intact
